**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE                                            Date Issued: 27 August 2010</mark>** 



# **ICSG Global Copper Scrap Research Project: Final Report Now Available** 

Copper scrap generation, trade and use are playing a key role to balance the growth observed in recent years in the global copper market. If the demand for copper continues the dynamic growth related to electrification, infrastructure development and urbanization observed mainly in developing countries, and led by China in the last two decades, then the domestic supply, demand and international flows of copper scrap are expected to remain important issues for all copper related business in the medium and long term. This report presents a comprehensive picture of the global copper scrap market and its determinants, synthesizing the findings of ICSG research project on the copper and copper alloy scrap market. 

This project allowed ICSG to improve the consistency, coverage and accuracy of our copper scrap statistics related to copper scrap use, trade and supply. A better understanding of the economic dynamics of the copper scrap market and its determinants was achieved, as well as the identification of the drivers of global copper scrap flows in regions with limited available information as such as China, India and the Russian Federation, together with a better understanding of the scrap supply and demand in Europe, NAFTA and the rest of the world. The report also presents a global overview of recycling and trade policy measures affecting copper scrap in OECD economies and Asia. The role of the displacement of secondary treatment plants of copper scrap from developed countries to China is reviewed in detail in this study. 

The Global Copper Scrap Research Project Report begins with a brief introduction to the global copper scrap market and defines the different types of copper scrap. Key drivers of the global copper scrap market are then presented in Section III in order to give readers a sense of what are the most important determinants of how the global scrap market functions. In Section IV, the overall structure and evolution of the global copper scrap market is presented, including information on copper scrap market usage, supply and market balance. Using the balance with the data on global end use of copper we look at the question of what is the role of copper scrap in the global copper market and a detailed discussion of the role of recycling rates follows for all countries with data available. 

The report includes a detailed analysis of the scrap market in China, followed by country and regional analysis of the market in Japan, East Asia, Oceania and India. A special section includes the European Union and Eastern Europe with an emphasis on the scrap market in the Russian Federation including scrap supply and use by fabricators and smelters. The challenges in creating a network of updated contacts with semis fabricators using databases developed under t
